Wheel Loaders — common questions

What is a wheel loader used for?

Wheel loaders are used for loading trucks and hoppers, moving bulk aggregate and recycled material, clearing snow, handling pallets with forks, and moving demolition waste across a yard or site.

Wheel loader vs skid steer — which should I buy?

Wheel loaders are bigger, lift higher, carry more, and travel faster across long yards. Skid steers are more maneuverable in tight spaces and accept a wider attachment library. Pick based on volume per cycle and yard layout.

Can a wheel loader run a snow plow?

Yes. With a correctly matched snow blade, snow bucket, or pusher box, a wheel loader can support commercial snow and ice operations on lots, yards and private roads.

What bucket capacity do I need?

Match bucket size to the truck or hopper you load most often. Oversized buckets slow cycle times and stress the chassis; undersized buckets cost cycles. The Konstructz team can size the bucket to your loading targets.
